# FAQ-002 Engineering FAQ #2
Revision: Rev A

Q1: What lubricant should be used for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01)?
A1: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-709 for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01). Background: This lubricant was selected for its compatibility with the cabinet materials, shot media, and seals. Rationale: Using the specified part eliminates variability that can cause premature wear of moving parts and reduces contamination of the blast media. Example: When replacing the supply on EQ-P3-L3-SB01, verify the container label matches CFW-LUB-709 before transfer. Records to keep: retain supply receipts and the equipment lubrication log entry that cites the container lot or batch linked to CFW-LUB-709. Refer to QS-PROC-10 for acceptance sampling and receiving checks.

Q2: What is the blast wheel liner bolt torque for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01)?
A2: Tighten blast wheel liner bolts on Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) to 105 N·m. Background: Proper bolt torque secures the liner to prevent movement during operation and maintains wheel balance. Rationale: 105 N·m was determined to provide sufficient clamp force without overstressing the liner bolt threads or the liner material. Example: When replacing a worn liner, torque bolts to 105 N·m in a star pattern to distribute clamp load evenly. Records to keep: document the torque event in the maintenance work order including the equipment id EQ-P3-L3-SB01, date, technician initials, and the torque value 105 N·m. Consult SOP-P1-L3-04 for bolting procedures and torque verification steps.

Q3: What lubricant should be used for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03)?
A3: Use lubricant part number CFW-LUB-725 for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03). Background: CFW-LUB-725 is specified for high-temperature-bearing housings and feed mechanisms associated with induction heating lines. Rationale: Specifying CFW-LUB-725 ensures consistent lubrication film thickness and protects components exposed to thermal cycling. Example: During scheduled servicing of EQ-P2-L3-IH03, drain and apply CFW-LUB-725 to the designated lubrication points as listed in the machine lubrication chart. Records to keep: maintain the lubricant change record referencing CFW-LUB-725, equipment id EQ-P2-L3-IH03, and supplier batch details. See SOP-P2-L3-05 for lubrication point diagrams and service steps.

Q4: How long should the spindle warm-up for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) be?
A4: The spindle warm-up time for Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03) is 27 minutes. Background: Controlled warm-up reduces thermal gradient across the spindle and bearings, improving geometric stability at the start of a production run. Rationale: A 27 minutes warm-up was derived from spindle thermal response tests and balances production throughput with dimensional control. Example: Before critical lots, follow the warm-up cycle on EQ-P1-L3-CN03 for 27 minutes at the machine default idle profile to stabilize spindle temperature. Records to keep: log warm-up start and completion times in the machine run log for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 and note any deviations from the 27 minutes duration. Reference QS-PROC-10 for production readiness checks.

Q5: What is the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02)?
A5: The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C. Background: The setpoint defines the target temperature for the austenitizing stage to achieve the desired metallurgical condition prior to quench. Rationale: 845 °C was selected to match alloy process windows and to ensure consistent phase transformation for downstream hardness and microstructure requirements. Example: When running the austenitizing recipe for EQ-P2-L3-HT02, confirm the controller is set to 845 °C and that the profile holds at the setpoint for the prescribed soak time per the furnace procedure. Records to keep: maintain the furnace run sheet showing the setpoint 845 °C, actual recorded temperatures, lot numbers, and operator initials for traceability. See SOP-P2-L3-05 for furnace loading and monitoring instructions.

Related documents: QS-PROC-10, SOP-P1-L3-04, SOP-P2-L3-05

Document control notes: update the equipment lubrication logs, torque verification records, machine run logs, and furnace run sheets as described above to support auditability and continual improvement.
